# Model card: CV parsing

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Read a structured profile from a CV: contact details, experience, education, skills, each with a verbatim quote. |
| Workflow | hire |
| Code | `pairly_hire.screening.pipeline.parse_cv` (engine: `pairly_core.extraction.engine.extract`, schema `pairly_hire.screening.profile.CvProfile`) |
| Prompt | `core_extract` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `af089775e5e1419c...` |
| Output schema | `ExtractionOutput` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 8192 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The sanitised CV text (guardrail findings removed) as a delimited data block, and the schema description. Only a `GuardedInput` built from the CV's own guardrail report is accepted.

## Outputs

Per field: a value as text, a verbatim quote and a confidence. Every value is checked in code: the quote must be in the text and map back to the CV, the value must parse and be readable from the quote. A failed check sets the confidence to 0 and flags the field.

## Human oversight

The profile is used for blind redaction and claim checks, never to decide. Flagged or low-confidence values are shown as such to the reviewer, and a screening that could not parse goes to a person.

## Limits

* Scanned CVs depend on OCR quality.
* Unusual layouts can split or merge sections.
* A value the model does not return stays empty; nothing is guessed.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

Numbers come only from result files committed in `evals/results/`, exactly as written there. See [evals.md](../evals.md) for what each run measures.
